title: Oil & Filter Service
subtitle: I'll stay with you step by step — short checks, big visuals, zero judgment.
tone: Live coach: warm, short, celebrate micro-wins. Max 2 buttons. GIF/video first. Branch on 'done' vs 'problem'. Trust nudge every ~3 steps.

ux_rules.trust_reminder_default: If you're unsure about anything, stop and go to a shop — that's the smart call, not quitting.

prerequisites: Engine cool enough to touch the drain area safely (warm OK; hot not)
Correct oil viscosity (door-jamb sticker or manual)

adaptive_rules.coach_note: Most gas engines on full synthetic: plan ~5,000–7,500 miles (manual wins).
adaptive_rules.oil_spec_hint: Use the viscosity on the door jamb (often 0W-20 or 5W-30).

adaptive_rules.coach_note: Hybrids still need oil — short trips create moisture even when the ICE naps.
adaptive_rules.oil_spec_hint: Many hybrids want 0W-16 or 0W-20 — confirm on the oil cap.

adaptive_rules.coach_note: Past 100k — nice longevity. Prefer the shorter interval and peek for leaks under there.
Newer vehicle — follow the first oil-change window in the manual.
Diesel needs the right API/ACEA class — don't sub regular gas oil.
This brand often wants OEM-approved oil. Unsure of the code? A specialist oil change is smart.
EVs don't take engine oil. Tell me if you meant another fluid and we'll switch.

visual_assets.alt: Oil jug, filter, and gloves looping gently
visual_assets.shot_description: 3s loop: soft pan across oil + filter kit. Warm garage light. No text.
Simple motion: mileage → oil can icon → checkmark window.
2s crossfade DIY ↔ shop. Friendly, not gated.
Items pop in: oil, filter, washer, funnel.
Jack → stand on pinch weld → shake test. Red X on jack-only.
15–25s vertical: crack plug → hand finish → drain. Gloves on.
Pour → idle → wipe stick → correct range.

visual_assets.alt: Safe approach for a stuck drain plug
visual_assets.shot_description: Penetrating oil → correct socket → stop before rounding.

steps.title: Let's protect that engine
steps.coach_encourage: You're already ahead of most owners just by being here.
steps.description: I'll confirm the vehicle, then we'll pick DIY or a shop. Either path keeps the engine happy — I'll celebrate the wins either way.

action_buttons.label: Update vehicle first
action_buttons.payload: Please update my year, make, model, engine, and current mileage before oil service.

variants.title: Quick check — may not apply
variants.description: Battery EVs don't take engine oil. Tell me in chat if you meant another fluid.
variants.personalize: Your {{year}} {{make}} {{model}} is an EV — engine oil service doesn't apply.

steps.title: Are you due?
steps.coach_encourage: No wrong answer — we'll match the interval to your car.
steps.personalize: At {{mileage}} miles, here's how I'd think about timing.
steps.description: Match mileage and powertrain to a sensible window. Your owner's manual always overrides generic advice.

variants.description: High-mile champ — lean toward ~5k synthetic intervals and peek for leaks.
Hybrid note: keep oil fresh even if the gas engine naps a lot.

steps.title: Let's decide together
steps.coach_encourage: Asking is smart ownership — I've got you.
steps.description: If last service is unknown, treat it as due soon and prepare parts. If you're within ~1,000 miles, buy oil + filter now and schedule. Want a precise call? Send last date + mileage in chat.

action_buttons.label: Ask coach in chat
action_buttons.payload: Help me decide if my oil change is due based on my mileage and last service date.

steps.title: DIY or shop?
steps.coach_encourage: Both are wins. Pick what fits today.
steps.personalize: DIY for your {{make}} is usually $45–$120 and ~45 min with safe access.
steps.description: DIY if you have stands/ramps and the right oil. Shop if tools, space, or OEM oil codes feel fuzzy.
steps.safety_warning: Never work under a car on a jack alone.
steps.trust_nudge: If you're unsure about lifting or oil spec, stop and go to a shop — that's the smart call, not quitting.

variants.description: Confirm OEM oil approval first. No code on the jug? Specialist quick-lube is wise.
variants.coach_encourage: Choosing a shop for the right oil is pro-level thinking.

steps.title: Parts ready?
steps.coach_encourage: Lay it out once — the job feels half done.
steps.description: Oil (viscosity + quantity), matching filter, crush washer if needed. Photo the oil-cap sticker if you want a double-check.

steps.title: Let's nail the spec
steps.coach_encourage: Better to pause for the right jug than guess.
steps.description: Snap the oil-cap / door sticker, or open parts for oil + filter matched to your garage profile.

steps.title: Make the car safe
steps.coach_encourage: Safety first — you're doing this like a pro.
steps.description: Level ground, park/brake, chock wheels. Stands on pinch welds, then a firm shake test. Watch the GIF once.
steps.safety_warning: Never rely on a jack alone. Hot exhaust burns — stay clear.

steps.title: Drain the old oil
steps.coach_encourage: Steady hands — you're in the middle of a real service.
steps.description: Pan under the plug. Crack with a wrench, finish by hand, let it drain. Keep the plug somewhere clean.
steps.safety_warning: Oil can burn. Last threads release a sudden flow.
steps.trust_nudge: If the plug feels like it might round off or you're unsure, stop and go to a shop — that's the smart call, not quitting.

steps.title: Stuck plug — slow down
steps.coach_encourage: Stopping before you round it? That's technician instinct.
steps.description: Use the correct socket (not 12-point if it's rounded). Penetrating oil, steady pressure — no cheater pipes. If it still fights, shop/heli-coil beats a ruined pan.
steps.safety_warning: Forcing a rounded plug can turn a $60 job into a $600 pan repair.

steps.title: Swap the filter
steps.description: Remove old filter (expect a drip). Wipe mount. Oil the new gasket. Hand-tight — usually ¾–1 turn after contact.
steps.safety_warning: Start by hand only — cross-threading dumps oil on a hot exhaust.

action_buttons.label: Old filter won't budge
action_buttons.payload: My oil filter is stuck. Coach me through safe removal options.

variants.description: Cartridge filter: replace all O-rings, oil lightly, torque the cap to spec.

steps.title: Refill & verify
steps.coach_encourage: Last stretch — you've earned this quiet idle.
steps.description: Plug + washer to torque. Fill just under capacity, idle 30–60s, shut off, wait, read dipstick. Top off gradually. Check for drips.
steps.trust_nudge: If you see a leak or the level won't settle and you're unsure, stop and go to a shop — that's the smart call, not quitting.

steps.title: Let's fix the level safely
steps.coach_encourage: You caught it early — that's the whole point of coaching.
steps.description: Low: add 0.25 qt, recheck. High: drain a little from the plug or extract — don't drive overfilled. Fresh drip at plug/filter: snug carefully, recheck. Still unsure? Shop.
steps.safety_warning: Active leak onto exhaust = stop. Don't drive.

steps.title: Log the win
steps.coach_encourage: You just bought quieter miles. Seriously — well done.
steps.personalize: I'll remind you before the next interval on your {{make}} {{model}}.
steps.description: Reset the oil light if your model has one, then save mileage + oil type to the health file.

action_buttons.label: How do I reset the light?
action_buttons.payload: How do I reset the oil maintenance reminder on my vehicle?

completion.title: Oil service complete
completion.coach_encourage: Proud of you — that's real garage ownership.
completion.description: Default next check ~5,000–7,500 miles (we adapt to powertrain + manual). Keep a photo of the jug in your health file.

action_buttons.label: Ask a follow-up
action_buttons.payload: I just finished an oil and filter change. Any post-service checks this week?
